subtitles.frontierhunts.deer_rub: Buck rubs antlers on a tree
guide.frontierhunts.lesson.sign.p4: Rubs and scrapes are only where a buck has actually made one, and you can watch him do it. From early September, when the velvet comes off, he walks up to a sapling or small tree, lowers his head and works his antlers up and down the trunk for 6 to 15 seconds, bark chips flying. The stripped wood is left exactly where his antlers reached.
guide.frontierhunts.lesson.sign.p5: From late September he also makes scrapes: he paws the ground bare under a low branch, works that licking branch with his forehead, antlers and mouth, then urinates down his hocks into the scrape. Sign peaks in the October pre-rut and early November, mature bucks make the most, and they come back to freshen their scrapes again and again.
guide.frontierhunts.lesson.sign.p6: A fresh scrape (dark, damp soil, often with a track in it) or a line of fresh rubs is a good place to wait or to set a trail camera.
